title: Multilocale Sanity Suite — CJK + RTL Heuristics and Spotcheck Prompts
content:
Purpose:
This working doc defines a compact, high-signal sanity/spotcheck suite for multilingual model onboarding focused on CJK (zh-Hans, zh-Hant, ja, ko) and RTL languages (ar, he, fa) plus mixed-script translation cases. The intent is: fast checks that catch regressions in translation quality, locale-aware formatting, and directionality handling before wider eval runs.

Scope and constraints:
- Not a comprehensive eval — small, high-precision promptset for quick PR-level or canary checks (run in CI or as a pre-rollout smoke test).
- Prioritizes common production failure modes: numeric/date/currency formatting, punctuation and spacing, bidi/directionality breakage, script-mixing, and short-context hallucinations.
- Each prompt includes: source text, meta (locale, domain), expected behavior, and scoring hints. Where helpful we include multiple acceptable outputs.

How to use:
1) Add the JSON prompt entries to the onboarding promptset repo (see linked PR).
2) Run the smoke suite against the candidate model with deterministic sampling (temperature 0.0 or nucleus with very low randomness).
3) Compute per-case pass/fail using the heuristics below; aggregate by category.
4) If fails exceed thresholds, block rollout and create a regression ticket (tag ML-1289).

Pass thresholds (recommended for canary gating):
- Critical categories (directionality, numeric/date/currency formatting): >= 95% pass
- Fluency/semantic correctness (translation adequacy): >= 90% pass on this suite
- Overall pass: >= 92%
Note: thresholds are intentionally strict because this suite is small and targeted.

Scoring heuristics (automatable):
- Directionality check: output must preserve RTL order for Arabic/Hebrew segments and not mirror punctuation. Use Unicode Bidi heuristics + presence of LRM/RLM control chars only when expected.
- Numeric/currency/date formatting: numbers should respect target locale conventions (e.g., Arabic-Indic digits vs Western digits optional if domain allows) and currency symbol placement. Check regex-based patterns per-locale.
- Punctuation and spacing: CJK should not have extra spaces between characters; punctuation replacement must match locale norms (e.g., fullwidth punctuation for zh/ja when applicable).
- Semantic adequacy: short translation should preserve meaning and named entities; automated BLEU/ChrF over tiny set plus specific slot-level checks.
- Hallucination: for queries that require factual recall of provided input (e.g., "Translate: The meeting is on 03/05/2026"), output must not add extra facts.

Promptset (representative examples) — each entry below is intended as separate prompt-case in the suite:

1) Simple CJK numeric + unit (zh-Hans)
source_locale: zh-Hans
source_text: "请把 12,300 美元 转换为 人民币 并保留两位小数。"
expected_behavior: Keep numeric meaning, format output with standard Chinese punctuation and use standard Chinese number formatting (commas optional). Example acceptable: "约为 88,150.00 人民币（按当前汇率）" or "大约 88,150.00 元". Must not output Western grouping like "12,300 USD => 88,150.00 CNY" without Chinese labels.
scoring_note: check for presence of CNY indicator and two decimals.

2) Japanese date ambiguity
source_locale: ja
source_text: "次のミーティングは 03/05/2026 に行われます。"
expected_behavior: Translate with locale-aware date ordering or clarify ambiguous format. Preferred js output: "次のミーティングは 2026年3月5日に行われます。" Avoid US-style month/day unless explicitly asked.

3) Korean spacing with currency
source_locale: ko
source_text: "총 금액은 $1,234.50 입니다."
expected_behavior: Convert to Korean-friendly display: "총 금액은 $1,234.50입니다." (no extra space before '입니다') and ensure proper thousand separators.

4) Arabic RTL with embedded LTR token (technology brand)
source_locale: ar
source_text: "سنباشر عملية التحديث غداً عند 10:00 AM باستخدام خدمة Redwood API."
expected_behavior: Preserve LTR tokens ("10:00 AM", "Redwood API") and render surrounding Arabic correctly without reversing embedded tokens. Output should not insert bidi mirroring that breaks token readability.

5) Hebrew punctuation handling
source_locale: he
source_text: "נא לשלוח את הדוח עד יום ה-12/04/2026."
expected_behavior: Date should be preserved or normalized to Hebrew-friendly format. Punctuation (dash vs hyphen) should follow localized usage.

6) Mixed-script: Chinese + Latin identifiers
source_locale: zh-Hans
source_text: "函数 calculateSum(x, y) 将返回两数之和。"
expected_behavior: Keep code-like tokens intact (do not add spaces inside identifier or rename), translate surrounding explanatory text.

7) RTL numeric style preference (ar)
source_locale: ar
source_text: "كانت التكلفة ٤٥٠٠٠ ريال."
expected_behavior: Arabic-Indic digits preserved if source uses them; if source used Western digits, model may choose either but should be consistent and locale-appropriate.

8) Punctuation width in Japanese/Chinese lists
source_locale: ja/zh
source_text: "项目包括: 项目A, 项目B, 项目C"
expected_behavior: Use appropriate comma/fullwidth delimiter: "项目包括：项目A、项目B、项目C" (zh) or in Japanese use '、' for item separators.

9) Short-string ambiguity (machine concision) — avoid over-correction
source_locale: zh-Hant
source_text: "註冊完成。"
expected_behavior: Simple English translation: "Registration complete." Avoid adding modal verbs or extra words.

10) Localization of ordinal indicators (en -> ar/he)
source_locale: en
source_text: "This is the 1st quarter report."
expected_behavior: Appropriate ordinal localization (e.g., Arabic: "هذا تقرير الربع الأول"), not literal "1st" with ascii suffix.

Error taxonomy (for triage):
- DIR: Directionality break — bidi markers incorrect, embedded LTR blocks reversed
- NUM: Numeric formatting wrong — wrong grouping/decimals/currency symbol placement
- DATE: Wrong date ordering or format (MM/DD vs DD/MM vs YYYY)
- PUNCT: Incorrect punctuation or spacing (extra spaces in CJK, wrong comma type)
- CODE: Code/identifier mangled (inserted spaces, renamed tokens)
- HALL: Hallucination — added facts, invented dates/places
- MTL: Meaning loss — translation dropped critical semantic content
- MIX: Script-mixing incorrect handling (e.g., Arabic + Latin mixing becomes unreadable)

Automation notes / tokenization pitfalls:
- CJK tokenization: models trained with subword tokenizers may split characters differently; detection of extra spaces should normalize NFKC and strip ASCII spaces between CJK characters before comparison.
- Bidi: run Unicode Bidi Algorithm checks on both source and candidate outputs; flag if visual order deviates in a way that would confuse LTR tokens.
- Normalization: apply NFC normalization before string comparisons, but do not auto-normalize digits if the test expects Arabic-Indic forms.

Onboarding runbook (compact):
1) Pull latest promptset JSON and add new candidate-case if necessary.
2) Run smoke-suite script (scripts/multilocale_smoke.sh) against model endpoint with deterministic decode.
3) Collect raw outputs and run automated labelers for DIR/NUM/DATE/PUNCT/CODE heuristics.
4) Manual review passports: any case failing automated heuristics gets human label (triage owner in collaborators list).
5) Post-mortem and corrective action: if failure is model-side, open regression ticket with examples and attach token-level traces.

Guidance for writing additional prompts (best practices):
- Keep prompts short (1-3 sentences) to make failures easy to attribute.
- Include at least one embedded LTR token for RTL languages to expose bidi issues.
- Include explicit numeric examples, currency symbols, and at least one ambiguous date format per locale.
- For CJK, include at least one example that tests punctuation width and spacing (e.g., colon vs fullwidth colon, item separators).

Labeling schema (for human raters) — store as simple tags: pass, DIR, NUM, DATE, PUNCT, CODE, HALL, MTL, MIX. Add free-form notes field in the triage sheet.

Quick checklist for PR reviewers (when changing tokenization, normalization, or locale codepaths):
- Run this smoke-suite locally and in CI
- Confirm no regression in DIR/NUM/DATE/PUNCT categories
- If changing tokenizer or normalization, run before-and-after diffs on a subset of canonical examples (we keep a small golden set in the repo)

Known open questions / TODOs:
- Should we prefer Arabic-Indic digits for all Arabic translations or only preserve source style? (follow-up: product decision required) — owner: Omar Haddad — ticket ML-1637
- Add a small set of long-form (paragraph) cases for CJK that stress wrapping and line-breaking (TODO Q1 2026)
- Evaluate whether to include locale-specific honorifics in Japanese/Korean translations for formal vs casual tone — need UX guidance from localization partners.

Appendix: quick regex mapping hints per-locale (for automation) — keep in repo as separate small file:
- zh: expect no ASCII spaces between Han characters: pattern to flag: Han + \s+ + Han
- ja: item separator '、' preferred over comma in lists
- ko: check for spacing before '입니다'
- ar: detect presence of Arabic-Indic digits \u0660-\u0669 and treat as valid alternate
- he: treat dash/hyphen normalization carefully around dates

References and links:
- Confluence: CONF-4451 (Multilocale evaluation guidelines)
- Jira: ML-1289 (Onboarding smoke-suite infra)
- PR with canonical golden set: github.com/redwood-inference/models/compare/PR-632
- Slack thread with triage notes: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C01ABCDEF

Notes to self (informal):
- This doc is intentionally compact — aim for <20 small prompts so CI stays fast.
- Keep one-to-one mapping between prompt-case id and triage ticket snippet so we can repro easily.
- We may want to convert some of these cases into unit tests that run inside the tokenizer changes CI.

If you have additions, drop them inline and ping me (@sofia) on the Slack thread above.
